label: rem:borromean-topological-confinement
title: Topological three-body inseparability
html:
Remark. Topological three-body inseparability

Brunnian property. The defining property of the Borromean link \mathcal{B}_3 is that every two-component sub-link is the unlink. The three components are topologically inseparable, yet no two are pairwise linked. Deleting any one of the three unknots in a Borromean baryon leaves a trivial two-component unlink. The topological binding of the remaining two strands collapses immediately.

Implication for topological isolation. An "isolated" component requires lifting one unknot out of \mathcal{B}_3. This configuration is unstable in the Borromean topology. The move that extracts one strand unlinks the other two: pulling on a single constituent produces three unbound unknots. This Brunnian property models a strict three-body inseparability.
